title: Noise dissolve material with a burning edge
purpose: Dissolve three.js meshes through a fractal value-noise threshold with a glowing burn front, on an integer hash so the GLSL noise and its JavaScript mirror agree, and animate it by one uniform. Use it for spawning and despawning, teleports, burning paper, magic and destruction effects.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE under WebGL 2 (unsigned integer GLSL and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createNoiseDissolveMaterial
exports.summary: The double-sided dissolve material; animate uniforms.uThreshold from 0 to 1; an unknown option throws TypeError.

exports.name: valueNoise3
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the GLSL value noise, in [0, 1).

exports.name: fbm3
exports.signature: fbm3(x, y, z, octaves = 4, seed = 0) -> number
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the GLSL fractal sum, normalized to [0, 1).

exports.name: dissolveEdge
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the burn edge: 1 at the front, 0 past threshold + edgeWidth, 0 while the threshold is 0.

exports.name: isDissolved
exports.summary: Whether the shader discards a fragment with this noise value.

exports.name: NOISE_DISSOLVE_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL integer hash, valueNoise3, fbm3 and dissolveEdge.

exports.name: NOISE_DISSOLVE_VERTEX
exports.summary: Vertex stage: object position and world normal, InstancedMesh aware.

exports.name: NOISE_DISSOLVE_FRAGMENT
exports.summary: Fragment stage: discard, Lambert light and the burn edge.

options.name: threshold
options.meaning: Noise level below which fragments are discarded; 0 keeps everything, 1 removes everything.

options.name: edgeWidth
options.meaning: Width of the glowing band above the threshold, in noise units.

options.name: edgeIntensity
options.meaning: Brightness of the front; values above 1 suit bloom.

options.name: octaves
options.meaning: Fractal octaves; more gives a more ragged front.

options.name: lightDirection
options.meaning: Direction toward the light in world space; normalized.

options.name: ambient
options.meaning: Share of the colour lit without the light.

limits: Value noise, not gradient noise: its blobs line up with the lattice axes at low octave counts. The noise lives in object space, so the pattern sticks to the mesh and stretches with non-uniform scale; coordinates must stay below 2^20 in magnitude. Discarded fragments leave real holes, but three.js shadow maps and depth passes use their own materials and still see the whole mesh. The edge colour is plain emission, not fire or particles. Lit by one direction uniform; scene lights, shadows and fog are ignored. Requires WebGL 2 (unsigned integers in GLSL). Written for three.js r155 or later; only 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
